strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-24172 in the scipy source tree at the buggy commit 1b2e87dbc681 by building scipy from source and running the developer's test_gh24172 in TestYeojohnson. The test must fail on the buggy commit and pass on the fixed commit. The numpy backend is the one to target, and the failing assertion depends on the buggy relative error exceeding rtol=1e-7.

build_commands: pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  # or: python dev.py build
pinned_because: numpy<=2.3: era ceiling at PR date 2025-12-28, inferred not documented; the test uses only basic array ops so a nearby numpy should suffice
scipy: not installed from PyPI; the repository itself under test is built from the buggy commit, since the fix lives in scipy/stats/_morestats.py and the test imports the in-tree stats module
matplotlib: omitted; it is used only for plotting in the PR reproduction script and is not needed by the test, and no constraint is documented

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy commit, test_gh24172 runs and FAILS: at least one of the four xp_assert_close calls (lmb=-14 and 16 with -data for precision loss, lmb=-20 and 20 with -data for overflow) finds a relative difference above rtol=1e-7 from the hardcoded mpmath references. On the fixed commit the same test PASSES with all four assertions within rtol=1e-7.
risks: The test runs under the xp fixture, so it is parametrized over installed array backends. Set SCIPY_ARRAY_API unset and run the numpy case; JAX and array-api-strict cases are not needed and may be absent.

The bug's trigger is a relative error that must exceed rtol=1e-7 on a value near 12.4. Precision loss from retaining the constant term may be far smaller than that threshold on some platforms, so the buggy failure is not guaranteed. If the test passes on the buggy commit, the bug is not reproduced on this platform.

The reference values are 17-digit mpmath results. Platform libm differences in log and log1p are below 1e-15 and should not affect the transition, but a non-IEEE or unusual-FMA platform was not stated in the evidence.
The fix special-cases all-positive or all-negative data. The test covers only those cases; the mixed-sign path is unchanged and is not exercised.
The empty-array JAX path and the JAX JIT behaviour were unresolved in the discussion and are outside this test. Do not expect them to be covered.
The residual sigma^2 pathology for tightly clustered data at zero was noted as unresolved and is not covered by this test.
The failure is numerical, not sanitizer- or architecture-specific as far as the evidence shows, but no platform was stated, so the x86_64 Linux default is assumed.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath computed at mp.dps=100, hardcoded in test_gh24172 per the test comment
oracle.why: The expected values are independently computed high-precision references, so the test asserts agreement with them within rtol=1e-7 instead of matching the old implementation's output.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The buggy code retains the constant term and takes a direct log of the variance for all-negative or all-positive data, so for lmb=-14, 16, -20 and 20 with data [10,10,10,9.9] the returned llf can differ from the mpmath references by more than rtol=1e-7. xp_assert_close then raises AssertionError on the first mismatching call.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed code drops the constant term for all-negative or all-positive data and computes the log-variance in the log domain, so all four llf values agree with the 17-digit mpmath references within rtol=1e-7 and xp_assert_close does not raise.
